answer: In an agent-run solar market, where output reaches its zenith at noon, every buyer, even one on a remote ridge, must lock 50 tokens for 30 days before its identity can bid. Each bond backs only one active identity, so a delta of 100 fake identities requires 5,000 additional tokens locked for the full period. Splitting funds among accounts cannot multiply bidding access for free: the attacker must finance every extra identity and forgo other uses of that capital.
